title: poot benchmark result record
description: One record per (framework, model, precision, scenario) cell. The harness writes one JSON object per line into results.jsonl. Timing fields come from the runner; memory fields come from the harness external sampler; the env block is written once per run into env.json (not repeated per row). Which binary, on which backend and device, produced a row is on the row itself (build_sha, binary_sha256, backend, device).

framework_version.description: Resolved version of the engine (cargo pkg version / pip version / llama.cpp git tag).

precision.description: Precision actually run for this cell (e.g. f32, bf16, fp16, gptq-int4, awq-int4, mxfp4, q4_k_m).

status.description: ok = measured; unsupported = framework cannot run this model/precision (see reason); error = run failed (see reason).

reason.description: Required when status is 'unsupported' or 'error': the explicit reason / error message. For 'unsupported' it is the refusal exactly as the tool reports it.

build_sha.description: The git sha the runner binary was built from, embedded at build time and reported by the runner ('-dirty' when the tree had uncommitted changes). Reported by runners built from this repository (poot), which must give it on an 'ok' row and on a refusal ('unsupported'); absent from other engines' rows and from an 'error' row whose runner reported nothing.

binary_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the runner executable that was asked to run, read from the file by the harness; null when the runner path names no file. Names the binary; build_sha names the source it was built from.

backend.description: The backend the cell ran on (poot: ptx, rocm or wgpu, as requested through POOT_BENCH_BACKEND and reported back by the runner; other engines: what they report, e.g. vulkan).

device.description: The accelerator the cell ran on, from the harness environment capture (env.json gpu_name); null when the host reports none. Part of a cell's identity for `bench compare`, with backend.

gen_tokens.description: Tokens generated in the timed run (fixed per scenario for comparability).

ttft_ms.description: Time to first generated token, milliseconds (median over timed iterations).

tpot_ms.description: Mean inter-token gap over decode = decode_span/(gen_tokens-1), milliseconds (median over iterations).

e2e_ms.description: End-to-end request latency, start to last token, milliseconds (median).

iterations.description: Number of timed iterations the median/stats are over.

ttft_ms_stdev.description: Stdev of TTFT across iterations (noise indicator).

peak_vram_bytes.description: Peak GPU memory used during the runner's lifetime, from the harness NVML/nvidia-smi sampler (external, uniform across frameworks). Omitted when unavailable, including shared-memory iGPUs.

vram_baseline_bytes.description: GPU memory used just before the runner started (other processes), subtracted is left to the report; recorded raw.

peak_rss_bytes.description: Peak process resident set size during the runner's lifetime, from /proc (external).

gpu_util_mean_pct.description: Mean GPU compute utilization (% of sample periods the SMs were busy) over the cell, from the external sampler. Low = headroom (idle GPU between launches/syncs).

gpu_util_peak_pct.description: Peak GPU compute utilization over the cell, from the external sampler.

cpu_util_mean_pct.description: Mean process-tree CPU utilization (%, 100% == one full core) over the cell, from psutil. Near 100% while GPU util is low points to a single-thread host bottleneck feeding the GPU.

cpu_util_peak_pct.description: Peak process-tree CPU utilization (%, 100% == one full core) over the cell.

peak_power_w.description: Peak instantaneous GPU board power draw (watts) during the runner's lifetime, from the harness NVML/nvidia-smi sampler (external, uniform across frameworks). Omitted when unavailable.

energy_j.description: Total GPU energy consumed over the cell (joules), integrated from the same power samples as peak_power_w (power_w * wall-clock dt per sample, summed). Omitted when unavailable.

energy_wh.description: energy_j converted to watt-hours (energy_j / 3600), for readability at bench-cell scale.

util_series.description: Downsampled (~1 Hz) utilization trace over the cell for plotting util-over-time. Each entry is [t_s, gpu_pct, cpu_pct, vram_bytes, rss_bytes, power_w]; spans all ISLs of a decode-curve cell (no per-ISL markers).

sampler_interval_ms.description: External sampler period; a coarse interval can miss a short-lived peak.

self_reported_vram_bytes.description: Optional: the framework's own VRAM number (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated, vLLM weight footprint, etc.) for cross-check. Not the comparison number.

osl.description: decode-curve (spec 115): the fixed output length (tokens decoded + timed) at each context length.

isl.description: decode-curve: top-level summary context length (the smallest ISL point, for the report/index headline).

curve.description: decode-curve (spec 115): one entry per requested context length (ISL), aggregated by the harness from the runner's validated raw per-token samples. Runtime validation requires exact requested ISL coverage before this row is written. The shape of decode_tok_s / tpot_ms across isl is the degradation curve.

isl.description: Context length (synthetic prefill tokens) for this point.

osl.description: Decode tokens timed at this point.

prompt_tokens.description: Tokens the runner actually prefilled; runtime validation requires it to equal isl.

iters.description: Timed iterations aggregated into this point.

ttft_ms.description: Prefill cost (start to first token), percentiles p50/p90/p99 over iters.

tpot_ms.description: Per-token decode cost = (e2e-ttft)/(osl-1), prefill EXCLUDED, percentiles p50/p90/p99.

itl_ms.description: Inter-token latency, token-weighted percentiles p50/p90/p99 over all decode gaps.

decode_tok_s.description: Steady-state decode throughput = 1000 / median tpot_ms (prefill excluded).

caveats.description: Per-cell honesty notes: precision mismatch vs the matched target, vLLM KV-pool inflation, warmup excluded, etc. FR-009.
